([[Gardena, California]]) | college = [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]] (2002–2006) | draft_year = 2006 | career_start = 2006 | career_end = 2023 | career_position = [[Point guard]] | career_number = 5, 15 | years1 = 2006–2007 | team1 = [[Colorado 14ers]] | years2 = 2007–2008 | team2 = [[BC Kyiv|Kyiv]] | years3 = 2008–2009 | team3 = [[Menorca Bàsquet|ViveMenorca]] | years4 = 2009 | team4 = [[Unicaja Málaga]] | years5 = 2009–2010 | team5 = [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] | years6 = {{nbay|2010|full=y}} | team6 = [[Sacramento Kings]] | years7 = 2011–2012 | team7 = [[Joventut Badalona]] | years8 = 2012–2016 | team8 = [[Shandong Heroes|Shandong Lions / Golden Stars]] | years9 = 2015 | team9 = [[Limoges CSP]] | years10 = 2016–2018 | team10 = [[Tianjin Gold Lions]] | years11 = 2018–2020 | team11 = [[Fujian Sturgeons]] | years12 = 2021 | team12 = [[BC Dnipro]] | years13 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team13 = [[NBA G League Ignite]] | highlights = * [[LNB Pro A]] champion ([[2014–15 LNB Pro A season|2015]]) * [[Chinese Basketball Association|CBA]] All-Star ([[2012–13 CBA season|2013]]) * [[Israeli Basketball Premier League 6th Man of the Year|Israeli Super League Sixth Man of the Year]] (2010) * [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star]] (2007) * 2× First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] (2004, 2006) }} '''Eugene''' "'''Pooh'''" '''Jeter III''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|dʒ|ɛ|t|ər}}; born December 2, 1983) is an American-born naturalized Ukrainian professional [[basketball]] coach, executive and former player, currently serving as a player development coach for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and assistant GM for the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland Pilots]] and was a naturalized player for the [[Ukraine national basketball team|Ukraine national team]] with his naturalized name being '''Yudzhin Dzheter''' ([[Ukrainian language|Ukrainian]]: Юджін Джетер). == Professional career == Jeter went undrafted at the [[2006 NBA draft]]. He played his first professional season with the [[Colorado 14ers]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]. In August 2007, Jeter moved to Europe and signed a one-year deal with [[BC Kyiv]] of Ukraine.[https://web.archive.org/web/20140905052718/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/14915/3735/bc-kyiv-nabs-guard-pooh-jeter BC Kyiv nabs guard Pooh Jeter] In August 2008, Jeter moved to Spain and signed a one-year deal with [[Menorca Bàsquet|ViveMenorca]] of the [[Liga ACB]].[http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/baloncesto/acb/es/desarrollo/1152468.html Eugene Jeter, nuevo jugador del ViveMenorca] {{in lang|es}} In September 2009, Jeter signed with [[Unicaja Málaga]].[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/58210/180/unicaja-fills-point-guard-void-with-pooh-jeter Unicaja fills point guard void with Pooh Jeter] In November 2009, he left Unicaja and signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of Israel for the remainder of the season.[https://web.archive.org/web/20150402164536/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/61663/hapoel-jerusalem-lands-point-guard-pooh-jeter Hapoel Jerusalem lands point guard Pooh Jeter] On July 21, 2010, Jeter signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]].[http://www.nba.com/kings/news/press_release_2010_07_23.html Kings sign Antoine Wright and Pooh Jeter to Contracts] In August 2011, Jeter returned to Spain and signed with [[Joventut Badalona]] for the 2011–12 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/88144/fiatc-joventut-badalona-tabs-pooh-jeter.html FIATC Joventut Badalona tabs Pooh Jeter] In September 2012, Jeter signed with [[Shandong Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/95263/pooh-jeter-inks-in-china-with-shandong-bulls.html Pooh Jeter inks in China with Shandong Bulls] In July 2014, he extended his contract with Shandong for two more years.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/126622/pooh-jeter-to-stay-with-shandong-flaming-bulls-until-2016.html Pooh Jeter to stay with Shandong Flaming Bulls until 2016] On March 21, 2015, Jeter signed with [[Limoges CSP]] of France for the rest of the [[2014–15 LNB Pro A season]].[http://www.limogescsp.com/csp-pro-actualites-details/items/eugene-pooh-jeter-rejoint-le-club-pour-la-fin-de-la-saison.html Eugene "Pooh" Jeter rejoint le club pour la fin de la saison] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402231934/http://www.limogescsp.com/csp-pro-actualites-details/items/eugene-pooh-jeter-rejoint-le-club-pour-la-fin-de-la-saison.html |date=April 2, 2015 }} {{in lang|fr}}[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/156049/limoges-announces-pooh-jeter.html Limoges announces Pooh Jeter] On July 14, 2015, Jeter re-signed with the Shandong Lions for the 2015–16 season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/168627/pooh-jeter-signs-with-shandong.html Pooh Jeter signs with Shandong] In October 2016, Jeter signed with [[Tianjin Gold Lions]] for the [[2016–17 CBA season]].[http://www.chinatopix.com/articles/102489/20161003/eugene-pooh-jeter-tianjin-gold.htm Former NBA Player Eugene "Pooh" Jeter to Play for Tianjin Gold Lions in the Chinese Basketball Association] On April 11, 2017, he signed with Turkish club [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] for the rest of the [[2016–17 Basketbol Süper Ligi]] season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/231748/pooh-jeter-signs-with-besiktas.html Pooh Jeter signs with Besiktas] However he did not play for them because Beşiktaş was banned by [[FIBA]] from registering new players and the deal could not be completed.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/232824/deal-between-besiktas-and-pooh-jeter-fell-apart.html Deal between Besiktas and Pooh Jeter fell apart] On January 1, 2021, Jeter signed with [[BC Dnipro]] of the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/pooh-jeter-signs-with-bc-dnipro/|title=Pooh Jeter signs with BC Dnipro|date=January 1, 2021|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 2, 2021}} On October 28, 2021, Jeter signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web|title=Ignite Announces Veteran Additions, Coaching Staff|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/ignite-announces-veteran-additions-coaching-staff/n-5759170|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 28, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}} On June 9, 2023, he announced his retirement.{{cite news|title=Eugene Pooh Jeter retires and starts a new chapter with Portland Trail Blazers|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/1514649/eugene-pooh-jeter-retires-and-starts-a-new-chapter-with-portland-trail-blazers/#:~:text=Eugene%20Pooh%20Jeter%20decided%20to,years%20for%20various%20teams%20worldwide.|work=EuroHoops.net|date=June 9, 2023|access-date=June 11, 2023}} == International career == [[File:Srbija vs Ukraina.jpg|thumbnail| Jeter versus [[Vasilije Micić]] as Ukraine plays Serbia in Eurobasket 2013.]] In 2013, Jeter helped the senior [[Ukraine national basketball team|Ukrainian national basketball team]] qualify for the [[2014 FIBA World Cup|FIBA World Cup]] for the first time since the [[Soviet Union]] broke apart, by being the team's leader in assists during the [[EuroBasket 2013|2013 EuroBasket tournament]], with an average of 4.1 assists per game. ==Coaching and executive career== On June 9, 2023, Jeter was hired as a player development coach for the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] and as an assistant GM for the [[Rip City Remix]]. == Personal life == Jeter is the younger brother of [[Sprint (running)|sprinter]] [[Carmelita Jeter]], a two-time [[IAAF World Athletics Final]] [[gold medal]]ist.{{Citation needed|date=October 2025}} == Career statistics == {{Euroleague player statistics
